WikiSkill's knowledge layer is the Wiki Layer (wiki/), which contains structured knowledge in patterns/ directory with markdown files documenting failure modes and successful strategies, plus evolution logs (logs.md) and skill impact tracker (skill-impact.md) [5:11][5:12]. The tracking layer is the Raw Layer (raw/), which stores immutable execution traces from training examples [5:11]. The Wiki Maintainer updates the Wiki Layer by consolidating traces into the wiki [5:4][5:5], while the outer-loop harness programmatically updates the skill impact tracker after validation gating [5:12]. The Raw Layer is immutable and only written to by the Inference Agent during rollouts [5:11].

hot: [4:36] The agent’s most distinctive capability is detecting when parameter changes are co-dependent, i.e., improvements that only materialize when applied together, which single-parameter sweeps systematically miss. In IMG-100, AMP (mixed-precision training) appeared to be a marginal speed optimization in isolation, but the agent recognized it as a VRAM enabler: reducing memory from 14.3 GB to 4.1 GB made deeper architectures feasible, which in turn made CutMix augmentation beneficial (enough epochs to help rather than hurt) and EMA stable (enough capacity to regularize). This chain of co-dependent gains (82.38%→84.03%) collapsed if any link was removed, as Claude Code demonstrated by never discovering AMP’s enabling role, capping at 78.59%.
